issues.failure_explanation: The assumptions permit unbounded Lipschitz terminal data and obstacles. For example, with zero driver, constant uniformly elliptic diffusion, no active penalties, and linear terminal data, the Markovian solution remains linear in x and therefore is not in a bounded-function class $C_b^{0,1}$. The asserted regularity class is thus unsupported under the stated hypotheses.

issues.failure_explanation: For the displayed Black–Scholes coefficient, the covariance has diagonal entries proportional to $(x^i)^2$ and is singular whenever a coordinate is zero; its smallest eigenvalue also approaches zero as a coordinate approaches zero. Hence it is not uniformly elliptic on $\mathbb R^d$, contrary to both Assumption (ii) and Assumption \ref{assumptionpde}(i).

issues.overall_effect: The showcased financial example and numerical model are not covered by the paper's stated theoretical assumptions, so they do not validate the advertised theorem in that model.
issues.title: Black–Scholes example violates uniform ellipticity

issues.failure_explanation: For the backward parabolic equation, the proper viscosity supersolution inequality at a lower test contact is $-\mathcal L\phi-f_\lambda\ge0$, equivalently $\mathcal L\phi+f_\lambda\le0$, as the paper itself uses later in (T5:1). Proposition \ref{apb1} uses the opposite sign, and the subsequent claimed upper bound does not follow from the displayed inequality.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reverse the supersolution inequality consistently in Case 1 and Case 2 and redo the associated algebra; this addresses only the sign defect and not the separate nonsmooth-surface defect.
issues.overall_effect: The basic obstacle-violation estimate and all later penalty and discretization results relying on it are not proved by the written argument.
issues.title: Viscosity supersolution sign is reversed in the barrier estimate
issues.why_classification: The sign correction is local and forced, and the intended smooth-point calculation then has the required direction without changing the claimed bound.

issues.failure_explanation: The assumptions bound the jumps of normal derivatives but impose no sign condition. A concave lower-obstacle kink, such as $p_b(x)=-|x|$ with Brownian diffusion, zero driver, and terminal value $g=p_b$, has $D_b=0$ away from the kink while diffusion creates a local-time contribution that drives the finite-penalty value below the obstacle. The proposition would incorrectly force zero violation. The proof's surface-avoidance step cannot remove this singular contribution; moreover, the quoted quadratic exact-maximizer conclusion is not supplied by Ekeland's standard variational principle.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must impose suitable signs on the normal-derivative jumps or explicitly incorporate and control the surface local-time terms, and then reprove the penalty estimate and all dependent results.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed uniform $O(\lambda^{-1})$ penalization theory is unreliable for the nonsmooth barriers admitted by Assumption \ref{assumption2}, including the paper's advertised unrestricted kink-type regime.
issues.title: Arbitrary barrier kinks invalidate the pointwise penalty bound
issues.why_classification: The proposition is false in the stated nonsmooth class. Repair necessarily excludes admissible kink geometries or requires a substantially new local-time-based penalty argument, changing a central advertised guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: It is easy to see that \eqref{scheme} implies the implicit discretization scheme

issues.failure_explanation: The pathwise equation requires every next-step random variable to be exactly affine in the Brownian increment conditionally on $\mathcal F_{t_i}$. The conditional-expectation formulas only compute the constant and first-chaos projection and do not imply that exact representation. For instance, in one step a terminal variable proportional to $(\Delta W)^2$ cannot equal an $\mathcal F_{t_i}$-measurable constant plus $Z_i\Delta W$. A martingale residual is missing, so the terminal condition and (scheme) generally cannot be satisfied together.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Introduce the missing orthogonal martingale increment or formulate the scheme solely through conditional expectations, then redo the error identities and stability estimates for that genuine recursion, including an existence/uniqueness condition for the implicit $Y$ step.
issues.overall_effect: The principal discrete construction is not a well-defined general BSDE algorithm. Theorems proved from its pathwise identity do not automatically apply to the actually implementable conditional-expectation recursion, and Corollary \ref{cor:final} switches to that recursion without bridging the gap.
issues.title: The pathwise Euler recursion is generally unsatisfiable
issues.why_classification: Repair changes the core stochastic recursion and invalidates the proof's exact pathwise error identity, requiring new proof architecture for the main discretization guarantees.

issues.failure_explanation: For $p>2$, membership in $\mathbb H^p$ controls $\mathbb E(\int|Z|^2)^{p/2}$, not $\int\mathbb E|Z_s|^p ds$. On a short interval there is no bound of the latter by $(1/N)\|Z\|_{\mathbb H^p}^p$; time concentration gives the opposite scaling. Thus the absorption step used to prove the uniform estimate for every $p\ge2$ is invalid.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove the $S^p\times H^p$ estimate using a standard BSDE energy/BDG argument that retains the time-integrated $L^2$ norm of $Z$, with uniform control of the penalty term, rather than introducing $\int|Z_s|^p ds$.
issues.overall_effect: The higher-moment a priori bounds used in temporal regularity, discretization, and local-time estimates are unsupported even if the earlier penalty estimate is repaired.
issues.title: The uniform H-p estimate uses an invalid L-p-in-time bound
issues.why_classification: A replacement a priori estimate is plausible but requires a contained nontrivial argument; the displayed proof cannot be fixed by routine algebra.

issues.failure_explanation: Substituting $\lambda=\Delta t^{-1/2}$ into the displayed bound makes $\lambda\Delta t^{1/2}=1$, so it does not yield convergence. Balancing $\lambda\Delta t^{1/2}$ with $1/\lambda$ instead gives $\lambda\asymp\Delta t^{-1/4}$ and error $O(\Delta t^{1/4})$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the general-case tuning by $\lambda\asymp\Delta t^{-1/4}$ everywhere it is stated; retain the resulting $O(\Delta t^{1/4})$ rate.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised parameter choice for the general $Z$-dependent case is wrong, although the stated $O(\Delta t^{1/4})$ rate follows from the bound with a different choice.
